decision.finding: run_once calls append_observations then load_observations (separate archive lock scopes) and publishes latest.json, audit_latest.json, anata_latest.json outside those scopes. Archive locking and atomic JSON replacement do not serialize archive-snapshot generation with final anata handoff publication. The regression must prove B can append and finish while A is paused at anata_latest publication; otherwise a blocked B or mere write-order check can make the concurrency test vacuous. The suspected equal-T stale overwrite remains UNREPRODUCED.
runnable_no_network_contract: Use disposable exact-SHA checkout, unique tmp_path, T, valid PIT rowB, and A child run_once(network=False,as_of_ms=T) on empty archive. Intercept ONLY A-child runner.atomic_write_json for anata_latest.json; signal A_ready before replacement and wait on bounded release event. Do not patch B.

While A_ready remains blocked, append rowB once; B run_once(network=False,as_of_ms=T) must finish with exitcode 0 BEFORE A_release. Assert B archive_records_loaded=1, appended_observations=0, and nested source_evidence[(etf,fixture_two_writer,scoring)].clock_provenance.effective.source_record_id=rowB; verify disk anata_latest.json equals B output.

Only then release A in finally; bounded join/terminate; assert A output excludes rowB, final disk handoff retains B rowB (not merely equal as_of_ms or last-write sequence), archive one row, no temp leaks. If B cannot finish while A paused, test FAILS as vacuous. Positive sequential C at T must preserve B. Capture exact SHA, overlay hash, child exitcodes, logs and non-skipped counts.
